decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, generating and organising ideas with visual methods such as mind mapping. Second, thinking flexibly: producing several approaches to a task and adapting as you go. Third, imaginative analysis: bringing creativity to how you read and interpret. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about putting creative methods to work in your academic study. By the end you will be able to use visual and mapping methods to generate and organise ideas, generate several approaches to a task and adapt when one is not working, and bring imaginative thinking to how you analyse and interpret sources.

Creativity is not a decoration on academic work, nor a gift that some people have and others do not. It is a set of methods you can learn and use, and it is named among the attributes universities and employers value most. These lessons give you methods you can apply to real tasks straight away.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: generate and organise ideas, generate and adapt approaches, apply imaginative analysis.

practiceConnection.academic: Creative methods are not a side activity; they are how good academic work gets started and kept on track. Every assignment you plan, every problem you work through, every source you interpret draws on generating ideas, staying flexible and reading imaginatively. Build these methods now and they serve every project of your degree, and the creative problem-solving that professional work rewards.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the advanced creativity course takes these methods towards innovation, enterprise and the creative attributes that graduate and professional work reward. If you want the foundations, the introductory creativity course covers what creativity is at university. Going wider: the same methods support Academic Writing, Researching and Revising, where you put creativity to work on real tasks.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Creativity is no longer a vague quality but a set of methods you can use. You can generate and organise ideas with visual mapping, produce several approaches to a task and adapt when one is not working, and bring imaginative thinking to how you analyse and interpret sources. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, creative methods are something you practise in every module. Each essay you map out, each task you approach more than one way, each source you read for what it could mean, puts these methods to work. The same methods drive creative problem-solving in professional life, where generating options, adapting and seeing fresh connections are valued everywhere.

courseReferences.title: This course draws on Excelling at University by Dennis and Abbott (2026): Chapter 13 (pages 239 to 242), Chapter 4 (pages 55 to 58) and Chapter 8 (pages 118 to 120).
